variants.headline: Party leader blunders in election debate
variants.sub: An election debate has included a blunder by {leader}, leader of {party}.
variants.body:
The leader of {party}, {leader}, has blundered in an election debate. The misstep is established, but the words involved and their effect on voters are not supplied here. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the debate event from a fabricated quotation or a claim that the election's outcome has been decided.

The gazette records the debate blunder without reproducing words not supplied to this notice. An error in a debate and a result at an election are distinct events. The report should not imply a measured change in support or attribute a particular response to the public without an adequate basis.

We defend {target} against an exaggerated verdict. A debate mistake does not erase the merits of a political position, and fairness requires more than turning an awkward moment into a complete judgment. Care in the public record is part of responsible administration.

variants.headline: A debate brings a leader's misstep
variants.sub: The party leader {leader}, of {party}, has made a debate misstep.
variants.body:
